clue.text: Study class has one good man-C.E., presumably

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a form is a school class
I is the Roman numeral for one
ST, short for saint, is the crossword's good man

explanation.surface: A student of a class with one virtuous clergyman of the Church of England.
explanation.walkthrough: C.E. is the Church of England; a man of the established church conforms to it, as opposed to a Nonconformist.
explanation.definitionFit: In English church history the term described someone who followed the established Anglican Church rather than a dissenting chapel.

clue.text: High-currency accommodation

parts.note: camp means exaggeratedly theatrical, as in high camp
s was the abbreviation for the shilling, an old British coin

explanation.surface: Expensive lodgings bought with lots of money.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling (s) was a British coin worth a twentieth of a pound before 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups of tents or huts provide temporary lodging for soldiers, holidaymakers or scouts.

clue.text: Renders void a terrible, sinful lie

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A dreadful, wicked untruth cancels everything out.
explanation.definitionFit: To cancel or invalidate something is to make it legally empty or of no effect.

clue.text: Native baseball players? That's for the birds

parts.note: a native is an oyster raised in British waters, especially at Whitstable
catchers are the baseball players behind home plate

explanation.surface: Asking whether indigenous baseball players are worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native' looks like a person but is the British name for a home-grown oyster. 'For the birds' sounds like slang for worthless, but the answer is birds.
explanation.definitionFit: These black-and-white shorebirds with long orange bills feed on shellfish on coasts.

clue.text: Error causes road hazard

parts.note: a blunder at the wheel endangers traffic, and the word itself begins with a weather danger for drivers

explanation.surface: A driving blunder makes the road dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening four letters spell a fog-like danger on the road, which the clue hints at while defining a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunder or slip is an error, the kind of thing that endangers drivers.

clue.text: Odds on the river being in metric measure

parts.note: SP is starting price, the betting odds at the start of a race
taken as written
the Dee is a river in Scotland and another between Wales and England

explanation.surface: Betting odds on the river being measured in metres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Metric' here means poetic metre, not the decimal system.
explanation.definitionFit: In verse it is a foot of two stressed syllables, a unit of poetic metre.

clue.text: So long a time after us in Customs

indicators.note: the letters that come after the word us are kept, so us is removed from the front

parts.note: usages are customs or habitual practices
taken as written

explanation.surface: Waiting an age after we have been stopped at customs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' works literally: keep only what comes after 'us' in the word for customs. 'So long' is part of the definition, as in 'it took so long'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something took eras is everyday exaggeration for a very long time.

clue.text: Lizard beheaded lizard

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is cut off the front of the word

parts.note: the iguana is a large tropical lizard

explanation.surface: One lizard decapitates another.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an old variant name for the iguana, a tropical American lizard.

clue.text: A writer, man 'n' boy

parts.note: Steven is a man's name
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A writer described as man and boy.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Louis Stevenson wrote Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson was the Scottish novelist behind Treasure Island and Kidnapped.

clue.text: Craftily tries to ruin, bid for another share-out

indicators.note: craftily means slyly or with cunning manipulation, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A crafty attempt at sabotage and a bid for a fresh division of spoils.
explanation.definitionFit: Dividing something up again, giving out fresh shares, is a new allocation.

clue.text: In France, words about the troubles

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for words is placed around the article

parts.note: mots is French for words
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: A remark about French words and the problems they cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In France' governs both pieces: MOTS (words) goes about LES (the).
explanation.definitionFit: To pester or harass someone is to bother or trouble them, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Weave or change position so as to daunt

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are told to change position, that is to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A weaver shifting position to intimidate someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimidate by a show of power or grandeur is to cow or daunt someone.

clue.text: Something pointed north-a road leads to the' plant .

parts.note: a spike is a sharp pointed object

explanation.surface: Directions: a spike, then north, then a road leading to a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like route directions; 'leads to the' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nard is an aromatic Himalayan herb, the source of an ancient perfumed ointment.

clue.text: A dire sort of order in old Turkey

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant version of it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grim kind of command from the Ottoman days.
explanation.definitionFit: It was a written decree issued by the Ottoman sultan.

clue.text: Of the flank-bone one found in one French lake

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: found in means the first one is placed inside what follows

parts.note: lac is French for lake
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bone of the hip discovered in a lake in France.
explanation.walkthrough: I (one) and LAC (French lake) make ILAC; the first 'one' goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective refers to the ilium, the broad upper hip bone at the side of the body.

clue.text: Press to have one piece of music taken' out of the Prom, perhaps.

indicators.note: to have here means to hold something inside, so the pieces enclose the jumbled letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a tune is a piece of music

indicators.note: out of order, so the letters of Prom are jumbled

explanation.surface: Urging someone to have a tune dropped from the Proms concert programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The Prom is a promenade concert, the BBC Proms in London. I and TUNE hold MPOR, the jumble of PROM.
explanation.definitionFit: To pester or beg someone insistently is to press them.

clue.text: Atomic revolvers.

parts.note: not guns but particles that circle the nucleus of an atom in the old planetary model

explanation.surface: Nuclear-age pistols.
explanation.definitionFit: In the classic picture of the atom these negatively charged particles orbit the nucleus.

clue.text: It's fruitful to exhort the actor to immortality

parts.note: O is the exclamation that opens an appeal or exhortation
an appeal to live on forever
Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian and Edwardian actor-manager

explanation.surface: Urging an actor towards undying fame is productive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O live, Tree!' is a cry urging the actor Beerbohm Tree to live forever.
explanation.definitionFit: It bears olives, so it is a fruiting tree.

clue.text: Places about 10 points south perhaps

definitions.meaning: places as in situations or locations
a bearing given in compass points describes where something is

explanation.surface: Locations roughly ten points south.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are locations: places, and spots fixed by a compass bearing such as so many points south.

clue.text: Flower of Venezuela.

parts.note: a flower here is something that flows, so a river of that country

explanation.surface: The national bloom of a South American country.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the great river that runs through Venezuela to the Atlantic.

clue.text: A Greek letter sent out to the would-be wise

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek character is dispatched to those who pretend to wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means wise or sagacious, often used ironically of someone who only thinks so.

clue.text: Troy's single beast

definitions.note: read as Troy is, the 's standing for is

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one, means single
a lion is the beast par excellence

explanation.surface: Troy has only one beast of its own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troy's' is 'Troy is': the definition plus a link.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Greek name of the ancient city, which gave Homer's Iliad its title.

clue.text: Bird leaves insect for fish

indicators.note: the bird leaves, meaning it is taken out of the insect's name

parts.note: the cockroach is a common insect pest
a cock is a male bird

explanation.surface: A bird abandons an insect to go after fish.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: " Ay, now I am in —— ; the more fool I " (AYLI)

definitions.text: Ay, now I am in —— ; the more fool I " (AYLI)

parts.words: Ay, now I am in —— ; the more fool I " (AYLI)
parts.note: a line of Touchstone's from As You Like It with the place he has come to left blank

explanation.surface: A quotation from As You Like It with one word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: AYLI is As You Like It; Touchstone says this on arriving in the forest of the play.
explanation.definitionFit: The forest where Shakespeare's comedy As You Like It is set completes the quoted line.

clue.text: Get right in, cheeky, be rash!

indicators.note: in tells us to put right inside the word for cheeky

parts.note: impudent means cheeky or insolent

explanation.surface: An order to barge in boldly and act recklessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without due care or forethought is reckless, unwise behaviour.

clue.text: Brown bread is the most popular

definitions.meaning: the ... of the town is the person everyone celebrates

explanation.surface: Wholemeal bread is the favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Grilled bread is browned bread, and the darling everyone drinks to is the toast of the town.

clue.text: Suffer like a miner

definitions.meaning: to suffer is to go through or endure something
a miner has to go under, down into the ground, read as two words

explanation.surface: Enduring hardship as a coal miner does.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure hardship is to go through it; split in two, a miner must go below ground.

clue.text: Is beriberi treated in this country?

indicators.note: in shows the country is held inside the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: A question about where the disease beriberi gets treated.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a country in the Horn of Africa on the Red Sea coast.

clue.text: Bird makes man lose his way

indicators.note: lose tells us to take the way away from the man's name

parts.note: Ernest is a man's name
ST, short for street, is a way

explanation.surface: A bird that causes a man to go astray.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the white-tailed sea eagle, the crossword's favourite bird.

clue.text: Depending on a body of soldiers

definitions.meaning: a detachment or group of troops forming part of a larger force

explanation.surface: Relying on a troop of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: conditional upon another event, and a detachment sent as part of a larger force.
